newsitem.title: JAPAN: Sharp profits up but slow chip sales cast a shadow.
newsitem.headline: Sharp profits up but slow chip sales cast a shadow.

text.p: Japanese electronics maker Sharp Corp. said Monday it made a modest gain in its group profit for the half year, but a sluggish global chip market was still casting a shadow over its business.
Sharp announced a group net profit of 24.23 billion yen ($216 million) for the six months ended Sept. 30, the first half of the current business year, up 8.9 percent from the same period last year.
A recent recovery in demand for its mainstay products, such as liquid crystal display panels and flash memory chips, eased some of the pain from a weak global chip market.
Group sales grew 7.8 percent to 865.36 billion yen ($7.72 billion) from a year earlier, Sharp said.

"Recovering demand for liquid crystal display computer panels helped support the half-year net profit. The damage from lower chip market prices appears to be smaller than that for other companies," a Sharp spokesman said.
But, he said, a plunge in global chip prices earlier this year still clouded the company's business prospects for the full year ending March 31.
